description: We don't gatekeep recipes round these parts 🤠 Here's my full sugar cookie recipe and how I make them, so you too can have soft and chewy sugar cookies that hold their shape.  My royal icing recipe is pinned to my page, so check that out too! SUGAR COOKIE RECIPE Ingredients: 3 cups all purpose flour 2 tsp baking powder 1 tsp salt 1 cup (2 sticks) cold unsalted butter 1 cup granulated sugar 1 egg 1 tsp vanilla extract  Directions: -In a separate bowl from your mixer, combine flour, baking powder, and salt. Whisk well and set aside.  -In the bowl of your mixer, add in the cold butter and sugar. Cream together on medium speed until it's just lightened in color and beginning to stick to the sides of your bowl, about 3 minutes.  -Scrape down the sides of the bowl and add in the egg and vanilla extract. Mix on low until ingredients are combined.  -With your mixer still on low, add in flour mixture one scoop at a time, letting the ingredients come together each time before adding more. Continue mixing on low until all of the flour has been mixed into the dough. Try not to overmix! Once finished, your dough should have a play-dough like consistency and not stick to your fingers at all.  -If baking right away, preheat oven to 350°F. -Roll out the dough to your desired thickness and cut out your cookies. Place them evenly spaced on a baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes, or until they're no longer shiney on top.  I reccomend freezing or chilling your dough before baking to make sure the butter stays nice and cold. Personally I'm a bit extra, so I freeze my rollouts, and then to be safe I freeze my cutouts too since the dough warms as it gets worked with. Whatever amount of freezing/chilling you find acceptable, do that!  If you're making dough to bake at a later date, you can wrap it up and store in an airtight container in your freezer for 3-6 months.  Disclaimer: results may vary based on things such as ingredient quality, environmental factors in your kitchen, and your oven temperature. Experiment and adapt this recipe however you need to! . . . #sugarcookies #cookiedecorating #recipe #cookierecipe #baking
transcript: So many of you have asked for my cookie dough recipe and here it finally is. I'll be showing you how I make my dough as well as giving you some tips and tricks on how to keep those edges sharp. You will need all-purpose flour, baking powder, salt, unsalted butter, granulated sugar, an egg, and vanilla extract. The full recipe with all the ingredient amounts is down in the caption. I like to start by adding my flour, baking powder, and salt into a separate bowl for my mixer and giving it a good whisk before setting it aside. In the bowl of my mixer, I add in cold butter and sugar and I start creaming it on low at first just to break down that butter a bit and then I'm going to bump up the speed. I do prefer to use cold butter when I'm making my sugar cookies because when you cream together cold butter and sugar less air gets incorporated which leads to less spreading in the oven later on. Once that step's done, which takes about three minutes, I'll scrape down the sides of my bowl and then it's time to add in the egg and vanilla extract. Mix this on low just until the egg is broken down and combined. After that's done it's time to add in that flour mixture from earlier. Keeping my mixer on low speed, I add in those dry ingredients one scoop at a time making sure to let the ingredients incorporate before adding more. By the way, this recipe is for a single batch of sugar cookies which yields about 20 to 24 cookies depending on the size of the cutters you're using but you can always double or even triple the recipe if your mixer is large enough. Now that you're done mixing, you should be left with a dough that looks like this. It should have a Play-Doh-like consistency and it should not stick to your fingers at all. To make sure my butter stays nice and cold, I do freeze my dough after I roll it out and then I freeze it again after I cut out my cookies. Frozen butter takes longer to melt in the oven which allows extra time for those crisp edges to set so the cookies actually hold their shape. If you watched this far, thank you so much and if you try this recipe, let me know how it goes. Bye!
